notes.title: MTP is off by default on MI355X
notes.body:
Speculative decoding with MTP is opt-in on MI355X. The MXFP4 checkpoint
can't load its MTP module until
[its config.json fix](https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4/discussions/1)
is merged. FP8 and BF16 can still turn MTP on with the speculative
decoding toggle.

troubleshooting.title: Timed out waiting for engine core processes to start
troubleshooting.body:
On nodes with slow weight loading, a cold TP2 start of the MXFP4
checkpoint can take longer than the 600 s default ready timeout. On the
validation node each TP2 rank took 380–450 s to load its weights. Raise
the limit with `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=1800`.

guide:
## Overview

[Qwen3.8-Flash-Next](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) is a
multimodal, ultra-sparse Mixture-of-Experts model. It has 125B parameters, 
including an additional 51B N-gram embedding table, while activating 6B 
parameters per token.

The architecture combines four main ideas:

- **GDN + QSA:** three of every four layers use Gated DeltaNet to compress history;
  the fourth uses Qwen Sparse Attention for precise long-range retrieval.
- **Gated Residual:** four residual branches dynamically control cross-layer reads
  and writes.
- **N-gram Embedding:** a 51B lookup memory adds capacity with little per-token
  compute and can be asynchronously offloaded to host memory. (note that offload
  currently only runs on Nvidia devices)
- **MTP:** the built-in Multi-Token Prediction module supports speculative decoding.

The checkpoint natively supports 262,144 tokens. Qwen reports that QSA reaches up
to 10.2x prefill and 6.6x decode attention-kernel speedups at one million tokens.
On GB300, TEP4 is the recommended full-tray configuration. On an 8x H200 node,
use TEP8 for the official FP8 checkpoint; plain TP8 is incompatible with its
128-wide quantization blocks.

## Prerequisites

- **Runtime:** use the nightly image, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` on NVIDIA or
  `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` on AMD, or the nightly PyPI wheels. Stable
  ≥0.30.0 runs the model, but this recipe is tuned and verified on nightly.
- **Hardware:** NVIDIA CUDA and AMD ROCm instructions are provided below.
- **FP8 memory:** the checkpoint is 172.78 GiB; it fits on a single GB300 GPU
  (288 GB HBM3e).
- **BF16 memory:** the checkpoint is 335.28 GiB. The validated TP2 configuration
  used about 190 GiB per GB300 GPU.
- **MXFP4 memory:** the AMD Quark MXFP4 checkpoint is 169.8 GiB; it fits on a
  single MI355X GPU (288 GB HBM3E).
- **Host memory for N-gram Embedding offload:** at least 51 GB plus
  runtime headroom.

The Install block above generates the nightly-wheel and Docker launch flows.

## Serving

### Recommended FP8 configuration on 4x GB300

Use the official
[`Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8)
checkpoint tested by this recipe.

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3
```

TEP4 is the recommended full-tray configuration — we recommend it over plain
TP4 because expert parallelism is consistently faster for this model. TP4 and
TEP4 are both validated full-tray configurations, including with MTP3.

To serve BF16, use the `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` checkpoint with the same
arguments.

### Single-GPU deployment on GB200/GB300

The model fits on a single GPU: the FP8 checkpoint on one GB300 (288 GB
HBM3e), and the NVFP4 variant on GB200 as well. Single-GPU TP1 suits
evaluation and development; multi-GPU TEP remains the recommended deployment
for serving throughput.

### Recommended FP8 configuration on 8x H200

Use TEP8 with the Triton MoE backend on Hopper:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3
```

Plain TP8 is incompatible with the FP8 checkpoint; use TEP8.

### Recommended FP8 configuration on 8x H100

H100's 80GB/GPU is not enough headroom for the 51B N-gram/PLE embedding table
— it relies on PLE CPU offload, which vLLM enables by default. Use TEP8 with
the Triton MoE backend; as on other hardware, expert parallelism is faster
than plain TP, and plain TP8 is incompatible with the FP8 checkpoint's
128-wide quantization blocks.

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3
```

Benchmark MTP with SPEED-Bench (`--dataset-name speed_bench`), not `random`.

### MXFP4 on MI355X

On MI355X, the MXFP4 variant serves AMD's
[`amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`](https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4)
checkpoint, which quantizes the routed experts to MXFP4 with AMD Quark. The
variant sets:

- `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, which turns on the AITER kernels.
- `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`, which fuses the shared
  expert into the routed-expert MoE kernel.
- `AITER_USE_FLYDSL_MOE_SORTING=1`, which sorts MoE tokens with a FlyDSL
  kernel.
- `--gdn-prefill-backend aiter_flydsl`, which runs Gated DeltaNet prefill
  with a FlyDSL kernel.

The default deployment is TEP8, and the TP strategy runs TP2. The checkpoint
also fits on a single MI355X (288 GB HBM3E), so TP1 with the same flags
serves one replica per GPU; the builder offers one TP size per variant, so
set `--tensor-parallel-size 1` yourself. TP2 leaves more memory for KV cache
and gives slightly lower per-token latency; TP1 gives more throughput per
GPU.

Validated on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-83c078d955cd6e0c63d3b12abe669c8de936a370`
with the builder's TEP8 and TP2 commands, and TP1 as the TP2 command with
`--tensor-parallel-size 1`. GSM8K is 5-shot over 1,319 questions through
chat completions with thinking off; throughput uses random 8k-token prompts
and 1k-token outputs.

| MXFP4 on MI355X | GSM8K | Output tok/s, concurrency 8 / 32 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TEP8 | 0.965 | 665 / 1831 |
| TP2 | 0.967 | 801 / 1384 |
| TP1 | 0.967 | 751 / 1282 |

### FP8 configuration on a 4x MI355X GPU
```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0

vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
--tensor-parallel-size 4 \
--max-model-len auto \
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9
```

MTP is opt-in on MI355X; to turn it on, add the option from the MTP
speculative decoding section below.

### Full native context

The checkpoint advertises a native 262,144-token context, which vLLM uses when
`--max-model-len` is omitted. Startup and bounded evaluation were validated with
this limit configured, but a single 262K-token request was not tested.

### MTP speculative decoding

Add the following option:

```bash
--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

### Offload the 51B N-gram embedding table

Builds containing N-gram Embedding offload can keep the N-gram lookup
memory in host RAM and asynchronously prefetch the required rows. The initial
implementation supports both ModelRunner V1 and V2. PLE CPU offload is required
for DEP, and also required for TP/TEP on 80GB-class GPUs (H100) where the
embedding table alone exceeds available headroom — optional only on GPUs with
more VRAM per rank (H200 and above). vLLM enables it by default; set it
explicitly with `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'`.

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 262144 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3
```

### Extend to one million tokens with YaRN

The checkpoint is native at 262K. For a one-million-token workload, turn on the
**Long Context** feature above: it applies the model card's YaRN RoPE
configuration under `text_config` (where this checkpoint carries
`rope_parameters`) and raises `--max-model-len` to 1,000,000. Evaluate
shorter-context quality before making it the default — static YaRN holds the
scaling factor constant regardless of input length.

## Verifying

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(api_key="EMPTY", base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1")
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8",
    messages=[{
        "role": "user",
        "content": "Explain how Gated DeltaNet and Qwen Sparse Attention complement each other.",
    }],
    max_tokens=8196,
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

A correct response should explain that GDN maintains a compact recurrent summary,
while QSA selectively retrieves important regions from the full token history.

## Troubleshooting

- **FP8 on eight GPUs:** use TEP8; plain TP8 is incompatible with this
  checkpoint. TP4 is also supported if GPU memory capacity allows.
- **Mamba-cache capacity error at startup:** keep `--max-num-seqs 256`.
- **Runtime OOM on large multimodal batches:** keep `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90`.
- **Out of memory while loading:** enable N-gram Embedding CPU offload, increase
  TP size, or reduce `--max-model-len` to reserve less KV cache. On 4x H100
  80GB, plain TP4 OOMs at engine startup without PLE CPU offload — keep the
  default `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'`.
- **XPU/TPU startup error:** these platforms are not supported by the initial
  implementation.
- **Pipeline-parallel startup error:** N-gram Embedding does not initially support
  pipeline parallelism; use single-node TP or TEP instead.
- **DEP startup failure:** DEP requires PLE CPU offload (on by default); DEP
  without it is not supported.
- **MTP memory pressure:** reduce `num_speculative_tokens` below 3.
- **PLE:** a network layer that injects N-gram Embeddings into the main model. 

## KV cache offloading

Offloading is available upstream since vLLM v0.30.0 ([vllm-project/vllm#57145](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57145)).
Validation used [Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8) on 4×H200 (TP4),
vLLM commit `d1b4028d7e`, the Python frontend, `--enforce-eager`,
`--max-model-len 16384`, `--max-num-seqs 16` and `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`.
Qwen validation used the FP8 variant with `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}'`.
Validation used `TieringOffloadingSpec`: 8 GiB total CPU tier, `blocks_per_chunk: 1`,
a persistent filesystem `root_dir`, eight read/write threads and `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`.
Three CPU-tier reloads and three filesystem reloads after restarting the server passed.
Reloaded responses matched the cold output, including the reasoning field.
The five-shot GSM8K diagnostic scored 31/32; this is a small sample, not the full benchmark.
These results cover this text-only configuration, not the builder's larger tier/chunk defaults or other variants.
